## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** Going back now returns the cursor to the row that was entered, in every case the description names. No navigation regression was found in the tested scope. Cursor position after Left/Backspace, PR head compared with base:

| Back from | PR head | Base |
|---|---|---|
| Submenu entered from its row (keyboard or click) | That row | Top row |
| Submenu the menu was summoned straight into (no history) | The submenu's row in its parent | Top row |
| Search result several levels below the searched menu | The branch it sits under | Top row |
| Menu opened through a `link` row with a `target` | The link row itself | Top row |
| Entered row now hidden by `when` or disabled | Top selectable row | Top selectable row |

**Verified:** `setActiveMenu` rebuilds the list synchronously before `placeCursorOn` runs, and the deferred `revealCursor` from that rebuild runs afterwards, so it scrolls to the restored row rather than the top. `navStack` has no other readers, and it is reset on every open, so no old string frames can reach the new `frame.menu` / `frame.item` code.

**Optional test improvement:** The `goBack` side of the change is covered only by regular expressions over `Menu.qml`. Two edits that break the behavior still pass the whole of `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` (126 `ok`, exit 0):

```text
placeCursorOn(itemId) { return; ... }    -> cursor goes back to the top row again
returnTo = returnTo   (frame.item unused) -> Back from a link row misses the link row (target's branch or top row)
```

Moving the back decision into `MenuModel.js` (for example `backTarget(items, navStack, activeMenu)` returning `{ menu, item }`) would let the history frame, the no-history fallback and a `target` link row be unit tested the same way as `nearestRowIndex`.

**Pre-existing limitation (not introduced by this PR):** `settleCursor` keeps the numeric `selectedIndex` across later `rebuildDisplay()` calls, not the item. If a guard result or a live menu edit arrives just after Back and hides or adds a row above the restored one, the cursor stays on the same index and so moves to a neighbouring row:

```text
Back -> rows [A, B, C], cursor on B (index 1)
guard result hides A -> rows [B, C], cursor still index 1 = C
```

Base shows the same shift for a cursor moved with the arrow keys. It needs a visibility change to land after Back, such as a guard evaluation still running on the first open or a real state change between opens. An unchanged cached guard result does not trigger it. Re-selecting by `itemId` after a rebuild would remove it, and could be a separate follow-up.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR head and base, plus the Qt Declarative and Quickshell sources the menu relies on. `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` ran unchanged on head and base, under Deno's Node compatibility layer rather than Node. Behavior was checked in a headless Qt 6.11.2 QML harness that runs the head and base `Menu.qml` functions verbatim against a real `ListModel` and the default menu, with the guard and provider processes and the UI geometry stubbed. No live desktop session was run, so on-screen scrolling and hover were not observed. The PR's files are unchanged on the current `quattro` tip, but the merge result was not executed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
